## Lessons from our previous project: tests and verification time (2026-11-10)
Source: two clean-up lots on Panthelia, our long-running Unreal project (UE 5.8, C++, about 7,300 automation tests), both closed on 2026-11-10. We carry over the rules, not the code. Each rule below cost us real hours once.

**What it cost.** In one week of November that project ran 1,333 headless test runs: 25.7 hours of machine time. 586 of those were mutation runs, each with two rebuilds. The pre-commit check took 334 s and the full suite about 15 minutes. After the two lots the same checks take about 90–105 s and about 6 minutes, with 37 pointless tests removed and everything else still green. None of the gain came from faster hardware.

### What to test in a 4-day jam
- **Test only logic that is easy to break and hard to see by playing:** scoring, save and load, state machines, generators, math. Everything else is verified by playing the packaged build.
- **Keep the whole suite under 30 seconds of test time.** A check that takes minutes stops being run.
- **Do not write tests that are not tests.** We deleted 37: scans of the source text, checks that a field exists, and copies of constants, colors and UI positions. They fail when someone edits a number, not when the game breaks.
- **No registers.** No test catalog, no list of "known failures", no exclusion list. A run is green or red, and a red test is fixed or deleted the same day. Our registers needed a full suite run just to be refreshed, and a stale one blocked the check before Unreal even started.
- **Read a test's body before deleting it; the name can lie.** Six of the 37 looked like layout checks by name and tested real behavior. Two reviewers caught it and we restored them.
- **Name tests by tier, and never let a test name also be a folder.** If `Game.Save.Validate` exists and someone adds `Game.Save.Validate.Slots`, Unreal's Automation tree keeps the folder and silently stops running the first test. We had one that had stopped running and nobody saw it, because a test that does not run does not fail.

### A test needs an oracle that can fail
- For every test, ask: **what wrong implementation would still pass this?** If the answer is "most of them", the test is decoration.
- **One check per fixture when state latches.** We checked two things in one session of a tool whose "write detected" flag stays set until the session ends. When the first check tripped it, the second passed for the wrong reason. Each check now runs in its own session.
- **Mutate by risk, not per test.** Break the code on purpose in 1 to 3 places per change (a wrong result, a skipped guard, an unwanted side effect) and confirm the matching test fails for the expected reason. Mutating every test was our largest single source of runs.

### Measure before optimizing
- **Get three numbers first:** Editor boot, the sum of the test durations, and the wall time. What is left over is overhead. In our 225 s check they were 37 s, 114 s and 225 s, and even the 114 s was inflated: each duration included a wait for the next Editor frame. The real work of the tests was about 45 s.
- **Measure the whole, not the part.** Booting without the startup map cut one test family from 273 s to 31 s, so it looked like a pure win. On the full check it was slower (254 s against 225 s) and one test failed, because other tests relied on what the map kept loaded.
- **Timings vary from run to run.** The same code measured between 87 s and 108 s. Compare two paths on the same tree and report a range, not the best run.

### Where the time really went
- **The engine's `Automation RunTests` path spends about 4.5 Editor frames on every test.** The controller and the worker talk through messages, and the worker closes each test on the next frame. A test that takes microseconds reported 9.4 ms. With a few dozen tests this does not matter; with thousands it was most of the run. If it ever matters: `FAutomationTestFramework::RunSmokeTests` shows the engine running tests back to back (`StartTestByName` then `StopTest`), and that is the pattern we followed.
  - Details that bit us when doing that: drive it from `FCoreDelegates::OnEndFrame`, not from `FTSTicker` (some tests tick the global ticker themselves); a test that queues latent commands must get a real engine frame before the first one runs; flush the logs written by other threads before closing a test; and stop the engine's Automation worker, because it also advances latent commands and can close your test first.
- **Editor boot is most of a small run.** Flags that helped a headless run: `-unattended -nopause -nosplash -NullRHI -nosound -nocrashreports`.
  - `-nocrashreports`: every ensure a test triggers on purpose spent 2–10 s preparing a crash report nobody reads (one test went from 13.6 s to 0.9 s).
  - The startup map: loading our test level cost 14 s of every boot. **Give the jam project a small, nearly empty Editor startup map**, not the gameplay level.
  - `bEnableUncontrolledChangelists=False` (`[/Script/SourceControl.SourceControlPreferences]`, Editor ini): it scanned all 26,000 assets at boot.
  - Join several test filters with `+` in one run, so boot is paid once.
  - Exit with a forced exit once the report is on disk: the Editor's orderly shutdown took about 5 s.
- **Filters match by substring unless anchored.** Start a filter with `^` and end it with a dot (`^Game.Save.`), or `Game.Save` also selects `Tools.Whatever.Game.SaveSlots`.

### Costs that grow with everything that is loaded
- **A tool operation must not cost in proportion to all loaded content.** One of our Editor tools hashed every loaded package on each call: 2.9 s per call, 741 s of a 1,031 s suite, and just as slow in real use. If a tool truly has to read everything, do it in parallel (`ParallelFor`) and keep the decision on the game thread. With that, and with the tools booting without the map, it went down to 158 s.
- **Do not key a cache on file size plus modification time.** Unreal returns file times with **one-second** precision on Windows, so two same-size writes within a second look identical. A reviewer caught this before it shipped.
- **Do not call `CollectGarbage(RF_NoFlags)` in a test.** It unloads every asset nothing references. The next test that needs the player content reloads it, about 12 s each time. Use `GARBAGE_COLLECTION_KEEPFLAGS`.
- **Watch how long the player Blueprint takes to load, from day one.** Ours takes about 12 s. We did not find out why; the log points at skinned meshes and motion-matching data loaded through hard references. Whatever a character Blueprint hard-references is loaded with it, every time it is needed. Use soft references for anything not needed at spawn.
- **A test loads what it needs and cleans up what it loads.** Tests that leaned on the startup map's leftovers, or that loaded a level and left it initialized, were the ones that broke when the environment changed.

### Verdicts and evidence
- **Decide pass or fail from the report, not only from the exit code.** Our runner cross-checks the list of tests it asked for against the list that actually ran, and refuses a run where they differ.
- **Guard against a silently small selection.** A typo in a filter, or a module that failed to load, gives a green run with half the tests. Require a minimum count.
- **Count error-level ensures in the log even when every test passes.** An ensure during module start-up fires before any test exists to see it.
- **Every run writes to its own new folder** with a small summary file. Never reuse a report folder.
- **When a suite fails and no code changed, compare the engine version in the two logs first.** Our engine updated itself from 5.8.3 to 5.8.4 overnight and broke four tests. For the jam: stay on 5.9.0 and do not let the launcher update it before submission.

### Working with agents and scripts
- **A second model reviews anything that guards data, and every finding is checked in the code before acting on it.** The one-second timestamp problem was missed by the author and by one reviewer, and found by the other.
- **One build or test run at a time per machine.** A build cannot link while an Editor process holds the DLLs, and a measurement taken during someone else's build is worthless.
- **Long commands run in the background and report when done.** No polling loops.
- **Windows PowerShell 5.1 reads a `.ps1` without a BOM as ANSI.** Accented characters in the script turn into garbage; ours corrupted a source comment. Keep scripts ASCII or save them with a BOM.
- **`ValidateSet` ignores case, `-ceq` does not.** `-Mode direct` passed validation and then took the wrong branch. Normalize the value once.
- **In JavaScript, `text.replace(a, b)` expands `$` patterns inside `b`.** A replacement text that contained a dollar sign followed by a backtick pasted the whole preceding document into itself three times. Use `split(a).join(b)` or slices for literal replacements.
- **Put one-off scripts in a file, not inline in a shell command.** Nested quoting failed on us more than once in a single afternoon.

### The short version for the jam
1. A handful of tests on pure logic, under 30 s in total. Play the packaged build for everything else.
2. Green or red. No lists of exceptions.
3. Anchored filters, one boot per run, a nearly empty startup map.
4. Before optimizing anything, measure boot, test time and wall time.
5. No tool call or test may cost in proportion to everything that is loaded.
6. Stay on UE 5.9.0 until we submit.

**Kit change (2026-11-10):** the kit `CLAUDE.md` now has a "Tests y verificación" section with these rules (plus "every test must be able to fail" and the script traps), so every agent working on the jam project loads them without having to open this log.

## Open decisions (owner)
- Moving assets between machines: GitHub LFS (1 GB free quota) or a cloud folder.
- AI provider credits: Rodin, Unreal Canvas, ElevenLabs.
- Team name and members (each with their Epic email).

## Reminders
- The Claude Code sign-in on ASSETS expires between Nov 15 and 18: run `claude auth login` on Nov 11 or 12.
- After the jam: `Tools/Devlog/Install-DevlogHooks.ps1 -Uninstall` on each machine.
- Start the EmbeddingGemma server with `D:\Models\EmbeddingGemma-2\start_embedding_server.bat` (about 1.5 GB of VRAM).

<#
Package-Jam.ps1 - Empaqueta el juego para la entrega de la jam y arma el zip.
Receta probada en UE 5.9.0 (CL 60351404) el 2026-11-09:
  - UAT BuildCookRun Win64 Development con -build -cook -stage -pak -iostore -archive.
  - NO usar -nocompileeditor: con plugins no-default activos (p. ej. AllToolsets) el cook
    busca <Proyecto>Editor.target y falla si no se compilo.
  - Config/DefaultGame.ini con bUseZenStore=False (en la maquina de assets el cook murio
    escribiendo en la carpeta de Zen; causa no confirmada). El script lo comprueba.
  - El zip EXCLUYE los .pdb (simbolos de depuracion, ~340 MB que no hacen falta).
  - Limite de la jam: zip < 1 GB, nombre TeamName_GameName.zip.

Uso:
  powershell -File Tools/Jam/Package-Jam.ps1 -Project D:\Jam\MiJuego\MiJuego.uproject -ZipName Equipo_Juego
#>
param(
    [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$Project,
    [Parameter(Mandatory = $true)][string]$ZipName,
    [string]$EngineDir = 'C:\Program Files\Epic Games\UE_5.9',
    [string]$Config = 'Development'
)
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'
$projDir = Split-Path $Project -Parent
$buildDir = Join-Path $projDir 'Build'
$logFile = Join-Path $projDir 'Saved\uat_package.log'
[void][IO.Directory]::CreateDirectory((Split-Path $logFile -Parent))

$game = Join-Path $projDir 'Config\DefaultGame.ini'
$zenOff = (Test-Path $game) -and (Select-String $game -Pattern '^\s*bUseZenStore\s*=\s*False' -Quiet)
if (-not $zenOff) {
    Write-Host 'AVISO: falta bUseZenStore=False en Config/DefaultGame.ini. Se agrega.'
    [void][IO.Directory]::CreateDirectory((Split-Path $game -Parent))   # proyecto sin Config/ (2026-11-11)
    Add-Content $game "`r`n[/Script/UnrealEd.ProjectPackagingSettings]`r`nbUseZenStore=False`r`n"
}

$uat = Join-Path $EngineDir 'Engine\Build\BatchFiles\RunUAT.bat'
$uatArgs = @('BuildCookRun', "-project=`"$Project`"", '-platform=Win64', "-clientconfig=$Config",
          '-build', '-cook', '-stage', '-pak', '-iostore', '-archive', "-archivedirectory=`"$buildDir`"",
          '-noP4', '-utf8output', '-unattended')
Write-Host "UAT -> $logFile"
& cmd.exe /d /c "`"$uat`" $($uatArgs -join ' ') > `"$logFile`" 2>&1"
$code = $LASTEXITCODE
Get-Content $logFile -Tail 4
if ($code -ne 0) {
    Write-Host "FALLO UAT (exit $code). Primeras lineas de error:"
    Select-String $logFile -Pattern 'Error:|Exception|Cook failed' | Select-Object -First 15 | ForEach-Object Line
    exit $code
}

$win = Join-Path $buildDir 'Windows'
$zip = Join-Path $projDir "$ZipName.zip"
if (Test-Path $zip) { Remove-Item $zip -Force }
Remove-Item (Join-Path $win '*\Saved') -Recurse -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
Add-Type -AssemblyName System.IO.Compression.FileSystem
$z = [System.IO.Compression.ZipFile]::Open($zip, 'Create')
try {
    Get-ChildItem $win -Recurse -File | Where-Object { $_.Extension -ne '.pdb' } | ForEach-Object {
        [void][System.IO.Compression.ZipFileExtensions]::CreateEntryFromFile($z, $_.FullName, $_.FullName.Substring($win.Length + 1), 'Optimal')
    }
} finally { $z.Dispose() }
$mb = [math]::Round((Get-Item $zip).Length / 1MB, 1)
Write-Host "ZIP: $zip ($mb MB)"
if ($mb -ge 1024) { Write-Host 'FALLO: el zip supera 1 GB (limite de la jam). Usar butler o recortar contenido.'; exit 2 }
exit 0

176	## Lessons from our previous project: tests and verification time (2026-11-10)
177	Source: two clean-up lots on Panthelia, our long-running Unreal project (UE 5.8, C++, about 7,300 automation tests), both closed on 2026-11-10. We carry over the rules, not the code. Each rule below cost us real hours once.
178	
179	**What it cost.** In one week of November that project ran 1,333 headless test runs: 25.7 hours of machine time. 586 of those were mutation runs, each with two rebuilds. The pre-commit check took 334 s and the full suite about 15 minutes. After the two lots the same checks take about 90–105 s and about 6 minutes, with 37 pointless tests removed and everything else still green. None of the gain came from faster hardware.
180	
181	### What to test in a 4-day jam
182	- **Test only logic that is easy to break and hard to see by playing:** scoring, save and load, state machines, generators, math. Everything else is verified by playing the packaged build.
183	- **Keep the whole suite under 30 seconds of test time.** A check that takes minutes stops being run.
184	- **Do not write tests that are not tests.** We deleted 37: scans of the source text, checks that a field exists, and copies of constants, colors and UI positions. They fail when someone edits a number, not when the game breaks.
185	- **No registers.** No test catalog, no list of "known failures", no exclusion list. A run is green or red, and a red test is fixed or deleted the same day. Our registers needed a full suite run just to be refreshed, and a stale one blocked the check before Unreal even started.
186	- **Read a test's body before deleting it; the name can lie.** Six of the 37 looked like layout checks by name and tested real behavior. Two reviewers caught it and we restored them.
187	- **Name tests by tier, and never let a test name also be a folder.** If `Game.Save.Validate` exists and someone adds `Game.Save.Validate.Slots`, Unreal's Automation tree keeps the folder and silently stops running the first test. We had one that had stopped running and nobody saw it, because a test that does not run does not fail.
188	
189	### A test needs an oracle that can fail
190	- For every test, ask: **what wrong implementation would still pass this?** If the answer is "most of them", the test is decoration.
191	- **One check per fixture when state latches.** We checked two things in one session of a tool whose "write detected" flag stays set until the session ends. When the first check tripped it, the second passed for the wrong reason. Each check now runs in its own session.
192	- **Mutate by risk, not per test.** Break the code on purpose in 1 to 3 places per change (a wrong result, a skipped guard, an unwanted side effect) and confirm the matching test fails for the expected reason. Mutating every test was our largest single source of runs.
193	
194	### Measure before optimizing
195	- **Get three numbers first:** Editor boot, the sum of the test durations, and the wall time. What is left over is overhead. In our 225 s check they were 37 s, 114 s and 225 s, and even the 114 s was inflated: each duration included a wait for the next Editor frame. The real work of the tests was about 45 s.
196	- **Measure the whole, not the part.** Booting without the startup map cut one test family from 273 s to 31 s, so it looked like a pure win. On the full check it was slower (254 s against 225 s) and one test failed, because other tests relied on what the map kept loaded.
197	- **Timings vary from run to run.** The same code measured between 87 s and 108 s. Compare two paths on the same tree and report a range, not the best run.
198	
199	### Where the time really went
200	- **The engine's `Automation RunTests` path spends about 4.5 Editor frames on every test.** The controller and the worker talk through messages, and the worker closes each test on the next frame. A test that takes microseconds reported 9.4 ms. With a few dozen tests this does not matter; with thousands it was most of the run. If it ever matters: `FAutomationTestFramework::RunSmokeTests` shows the engine running tests back to back (`StartTestByName` then `StopTest`), and that is the pattern we followed.
201	  - Details that bit us when doing that: drive it from `FCoreDelegates::OnEndFrame`, not from `FTSTicker` (some tests tick the global ticker themselves); a test that queues latent commands must get a real engine frame before the first one runs; flush the logs written by other threads before closing a test; and stop the engine's Automation worker, because it also advances latent commands and can close your test first.
202	- **Editor boot is most of a small run.** Flags that helped a headless run: `-unattended -nopause -nosplash -NullRHI -nosound -nocrashreports`.
203	  - `-nocrashreports`: every ensure a test triggers on purpose spent 2–10 s preparing a crash report nobody reads (one test went from 13.6 s to 0.9 s).
204	  - The startup map: loading our test level cost 14 s of every boot. **Give the jam project a small, nearly empty Editor startup map**, not the gameplay level.
205	  - `bEnableUncontrolledChangelists=False` (`[/Script/SourceControl.SourceControlPreferences]`, Editor ini): it scanned all 26,000 assets at boot.
206	  - Join several test filters with `+` in one run, so boot is paid once.
207	  - Exit with a forced exit once the report is on disk: the Editor's orderly shutdown took about 5 s.
208	- **Filters match by substring unless anchored.** Start a filter with `^` and end it with a dot (`^Game.Save.`), or `Game.Save` also selects `Tools.Whatever.Game.SaveSlots`.
209	
210	### Costs that grow with everything that is loaded
211	- **A tool operation must not cost in proportion to all loaded content.** One of our Editor tools hashed every loaded package on each call: 2.9 s per call, 741 s of a 1,031 s suite, and just as slow in real use. If a tool truly has to read everything, do it in parallel (`ParallelFor`) and keep the decision on the game thread. With that, and with the tools booting without the map, it went down to 158 s.
212	- **Do not key a cache on file size plus modification time.** Unreal returns file times with **one-second** precision on Windows, so two same-size writes within a second look identical. A reviewer caught this before it shipped.
213	- **Do not call `CollectGarbage(RF_NoFlags)` in a test.** It unloads every asset nothing references. The next test that needs the player content reloads it, about 12 s each time. Use `GARBAGE_COLLECTION_KEEPFLAGS`.
214	- **Watch how long the player Blueprint takes to load, from day one.** Ours takes about 12 s. We did not find out why; the log points at skinned meshes and motion-matching data loaded through hard references. Whatever a character Blueprint hard-references is loaded with it, every time it is needed. Use soft references for anything not needed at spawn.
215	- **A test loads what it needs and cleans up what it loads.** Tests that leaned on the startup map's leftovers, or that loaded a level and left it initialized, were the ones that broke when the environment changed.
216	
217	### Verdicts and evidence
218	- **Decide pass or fail from the report, not only from the exit code.** Our runner cross-checks the list of tests it asked for against the list that actually ran, and refuses a run where they differ.
219	- **Guard against a silently small selection.** A typo in a filter, or a module that failed to load, gives a green run with half the tests. Require a minimum count.
220	- **Count error-level ensures in the log even when every test passes.** An ensure during module start-up fires before any test exists to see it.
221	- **Every run writes to its own new folder** with a small summary file. Never reuse a report folder.
222	- **When a suite fails and no code changed, compare the engine version in the two logs first.** Our engine updated itself from 5.8.3 to 5.8.4 overnight and broke four tests. For the jam: stay on 5.9.0 and do not let the launcher update it before submission.
223	
224	### Working with agents and scripts
225	- **A second model reviews anything that guards data, and every finding is checked in the code before acting on it.** The one-second timestamp problem was missed by the author and by one reviewer, and found by the other.
226	- **One build or test run at a time per machine.** A build cannot link while an Editor process holds the DLLs, and a measurement taken during someone else's build is worthless.
227	- **Long commands run in the background and report when done.** No polling loops.
228	- **Windows PowerShell 5.1 reads a `.ps1` without a BOM as ANSI.** Accented characters in the script turn into garbage; ours corrupted a source comment. Keep scripts ASCII or save them with a BOM.
229	- **`ValidateSet` ignores case, `-ceq` does not.** `-Mode direct` passed validation and then took the wrong branch. Normalize the value once.
230	- **In JavaScript, `text.replace(a, b)` expands `$` patterns inside `b`.** A replacement text that contained a dollar sign followed by a backtick pasted the whole preceding document into itself three times. Use `split(a).join(b)` or slices for literal replacements.
231	- **Put one-off scripts in a file, not inline in a shell command.** Nested quoting failed on us more than once in a single afternoon.
232	
233	### The short version for the jam
234	1. A handful of tests on pure logic, under 30 s in total. Play the packaged build for everything else.
235	2. Green or red. No lists of exceptions.
236	3. Anchored filters, one boot per run, a nearly empty startup map.
237	4. Before optimizing anything, measure boot, test time and wall time.
238	5. No tool call or test may cost in proportion to everything that is loaded.
239	6. Stay on UE 5.9.0 until we submit.
240	
241	**Kit change (2026-11-10):** the kit `CLAUDE.md` now has a "Tests y verificación" section with these rules (plus "every test must be able to fail" and the script traps), so every agent working on the jam project loads them without having to open this log.

## Plan de hoy

1. **Proyecto:** `C:\GameJam\Glyphbound\` en C++ desde la plantilla en blanco (no la de primera persona de Epic), con los plugins no usados apagados y el arranque del Editor medido antes y después.
2. **Jugador:** moverse, saltar, doble salto y dash, con vida y maná que regeneran y las teclas del GDD §9.
3. **Combate:** bastón con ataque básico, pistola y cambio entre ambos; Fireball con todos sus parámetros en datos y dos entradas de 0 a 1 (potencia y alcance) que mañana alimenta el QTE.
4. **Eras:** un mapa de prueba con portal y fundido que alterna pasado y futuro; manos en pixel art generadas como placeholder.
5. **Cierre:** tests solo de lógica pura, empaquetar `TeamTBD_Glyphbound`, `New-DevlogDay.ps1` y `Design/HANDOFF.md`.

## Lo que doy por hecho (corrígeme si no)

- **Git no guarda `Content/`** (decisión del equipo en `.gitignore`). Pondré en código y archivos de texto todo lo que pueda, para que quede en el historial. Lo que sea asset binario (el mapa, por ejemplo) vivirá solo en CENTRAL.
- **Arrancar el `.exe` empaquetado para comprobar que carga y cierra** no cuenta como PIE, así que lo haré yo. Jugarlo de verdad te lo pido a ti.
- **La estructura base del proyecto la escribo yo directamente** (`.uproject`, módulos, configuración) y lo anoto como excepción en la bitácora. Los sistemas de juego van a Muse Spark por `Invoke-LoggedAgent.ps1`.
- **El primer commit incluye lo pendiente:** el cambio sin confirmar de `Devlog/PREJAM_PREP.md` y `Devlog/raw/`.
- **DLSS no entra hoy.** El plugin no está instalado en el motor; lo reviso el día 2 y te pediré permiso antes de descargar nada.

## Una pregunta que no bloquea

La tarea de copia diaria `JamContentBackup` sigue desactivada y apunta a una carpeta de ejemplo. Como `Content/` no va a git, esa copia es el único respaldo del mapa y los assets. ¿La activas tú cuando exista el proyecto, o la edito y activo yo?

Aún no he comprobado que Muse Spark responda por OpenCode (está instalado, v2.2.7); será lo primero que pruebe al delegar.
